About the author

Lauren Roberts

20 books65.1k followers
When Lauren Roberts isn't writing about fantasy worlds and bantering love interests, she can likely be found burrowed in bed reading about them. Lauren has lived in Michigan her whole life, which makes her very familiar with potholes, snow, and various lake activities. She has the hobbies of both a grandmother and a child: knitting, laser tag, hammocking, word searches, and coloring. Powerless is her first novel (now a New York Times Best Seller), and she hopes to have the privilege of writing pretty words for the rest of her life. If you enjoy ranting, reading, and writing, Lauren can be found on both TikTok and Instagram @Laurenrobertslibrary for your entertainment.

i am so fucking disappointed in Lauren Roberts. like genuinely, viscerally, soul-deep disappointed.

i just finished the Powerless trilogy and the only logical conclusion i’ve come to is that Lauren Roberts is a thief. not metaphorically. not playfully. i mean a straight-up, copy-paste, no-shame thief. she hasn’t just borrowed tropes; she’s lifted entire plots, worldbuilding systems, character arcs, even dialogue—from not one, not two, not even three, but five wildly popular fantasy/dystopian series. and she’s parading them around like they’re original. like we haven’t read the very stories she’s plagiarized—just with different names.

the books in question:
The Hunger Games,
Red Queen,
The Selection,
Dance of Thieves,
and now, The Serpent and the Wings of Night.

let’s break it down:

1. The Hunger Games (Suzanne Collins)
(which, by the way, is one of my favorite series of all time; so yes, i noticed every. single. rip-off.)

(1) The Hunger Games” vs. “The Purging Trials” – let’s talk about “The Purging Trials”—a blatant, shameless knock-off of the Hunger Games arena. teens battling to the death for survival while being broadcasted live for public entertainment? sound familiar?

(2) in Powerless, the trials are broadcasted, and participants can win favor from the audience for rewards. literally sponsorships. she didn’t even try to hide it.

(3) the societal divide: Elites vs. Ordinaries? ok, hi again Capitol vs. Districts.

(4) Paedyn being good at archery because her dad taught her? a direct Katniss knockoff.

(5) and oh, the favorite color scene. she deadass copied one of the most tender moments between Peeta and Katniss and slapped it in like no one would notice.
it was soul-crushing when suzanne did it with green and orange but lauren just made a cheap copy.



2. The Selection (Kiera Cass)


(1) the name of the kingdom in The Selection is “Illeá.” In Powerless? “Illya.” i can’t even make this up. cuz apparently, even changing a single letter is enough to pass it off as different.

(2) the whole love triangle setup. been there, read that (wasn’t great the first time, was terrible the second)

(3) the rebellious father backstory—just like America’s dad in The Selection.

(4) and ofc, the classic “i’m not like other girls” moment where she wears a different colored dress at the royal ball so she stands out. r we serious?



3. Red Queen (Victoria Aveyard)

(1) the entire foundation of the world in Powerless is a carbon copy of Red Queen. society divided by those with powers (Elites/Silvers) vs. those without (Ordinaries/Reds). powers = privilege. lack thereof = oppression. copy. paste.

(2) Paedyn pretending to have powers so she can survive in elite society? that is Mare Barrow’s whole plotline.

(3) resistance movement? underground rebellion? also stolen.

(4) she even gave pae silver hair. come on.

(5) and the sweet, nurturing best friend/sister who sews clothes? (adena) v have alr seen this exact character already. MULTIPLE times.



IN RECKLESS:

4. Dance of Thieves (Mary E. Pearson)

(1) Captor vs Captive Turned Lovers Trope:
in Dance of Thieves, Kazi (the FMC) and Jase (the MMC) are enemies who end up chained together, forced to survive side by side—and obviously catch feelings in the process. in Reckless, Paedyn and Kai are… wait for it… forced together, on the run, enemies-to-lovers, while constantly questioning each other’s motives. the same dynamic. the same slow-burn trust. the same suspicious angst. even the same “let’s sleep back-to-back in the wilderness” kind of vibes.

(2) Kazi hides who she really is and what she’s doing. so does Paedyn.
Jase hides his plans. so does Kai.
everyone’s playing some undercover game while flirting and making vague threats. the “we’re both lying to each other but somehow falling in love” thing? yea, Roberts just copied it.

(3) MMC similarities: Jase is the leader of a powerful outlaw family ruling a feared territory. in Reckless, Kai is the Enforcer—basically royalty in the most brutal, fearsome way. both are boys with titles, knives, and emotional walls. both are feared. both are wanted. both are soft only for the main girl.

(4)The Desert Survival Vibe: a lot of Dance of Thieves takes place in rugged, dangerous territory. guess what we get in Reckless? the exact same unforgiving journey through wastelands, hostile environments, and constant physical challenges that magically draw the couple closer. HOWWWWWW original.




AND NOW FINALLY, IN FEARLESS:

5. The Serpent and the Wings of Night (Carissa Broadbent)

(1) Paedyn finds out she’s secretly royalty? just like Oraya.

(2) and the final trial ends up with Paedyn and Kai fighting each other—just like Oraya and Raihn being forced to go head-to-head.

(3) the vibes? the dynamic? the whole “forced to fight the one you love in a death trial”? yep. stolen yet again.



it is not even subtle. it’s not like “inspired by” or “a nod to.” it’s blatant. it’s lazy. it’s disrespectful to the authors who actually built these worlds from scratch.

what annoys me more is that powerless is being hyped up as this “original, groundbreaking” series by people who either haven’t read the other books or just don’t care that it’s a collage of plagiarism.

Lauren, if you’re gonna steal, the least you could do is not get caught. but you did.

and we noticed.

I have been thinking on how to review this book. On one hand, it wasn't as good as some of the people said it was, but honestly, it wasn't a bad book by any means. Yes, some things were handled very poorly, but others were done very well. Powerless was an enjoyable experience for me, but I wanted more from it, Powerful was simply heartbreaking and amazing, Reckless was a heavy victim of the second book syndrome, and Fearless was an enjoyable experience tainted by poor execution. Lauren has the potential to write really good books, there are some scenes in the book which are so beautifully written and the novella 'Powerful' showed a lot of what she can do with a good story. After 'Reckless' my expectations for this book were low, but tbh I was enjoying the first half so much—like honestly, I did not have any problems because I was vibing with the book. Me and Rowan both were having fun at the start, and honestly, the romance in this one was going really well too. There were occasional bomb drops of the word 'Pretend' that made my eye twitch, but they were not enough to make me hate it. It was looking out to be 4 stars, but the second half changed so much for me.

The pacing, for one, bothered me a lot. At times I would be so invested, but then there would be moments where I wanted it to move along and wrap it up because I felt like it was dragging. She paced this so viciously because those dragged moments would actually make me want to stop, but then a scene would drop that would have me so invested that it just bothered me. The repetitive nature in this part increased, and the 'Pretend' in this part made me wanna dnf this book!!! Like synonyms exist!!! One Google search!!! The plot twists for the sake of shocking us and them serving no purpose were there—one of them made me gag and I hated it. It really flipped the story and made me disgusted. But honestly, there was just so much going (not in a good way), and it felt like Lauren was having trouble grasping it. But besides that, the ending was satisfying and the epilogue was very sweet, even the one at the very end.

The romance, I must say, Kai in the first two books wasn't my favorite, but he was so good in this. He played the desperate-for-her part so well, and the chemistry between these two was so on point. Every interaction that they shared enhanced the book. Their thoughts about each other were raw and intense that it actually made me fall in love just by reading them. From a romantic perspective, this book really delivered because the forbidden nature of this book provided us with so much angst and longing that we deserved, and it just hit in all the right spots. There wasn't miscommunication, there wasn't any denial—it was all there, and it felt so natural between them. Honestly, the romance for me made the book worth reading because it was building up to what it executed, and I can't praise it enough for that. Like, the scenes that me and Rowan talked about were sooo good, like the good things about this book that we talked about was the romance... the other was just venting out our frustration.

SPOILERS!!
SPOILERS!!
SPOILERS!!

The characters, Kitt was very frustrating to deal with because my emotions were changing about him at such a rapid pace, but I never fully settled on anything other than frustration and annoyance. Every scene of his was so eye-roll worthy, and the plot twist she pulled with him actually being bad through made me more mad. And the thing that was my last straw would be how he threw such a big tantrum—like A BIG ASS TANTRUM—only for him to say 'I hope you both love each other' at the end as he died. LIKE BITCH WHY WERE YOU WHINING THEN. Paedyn was really good in this one. I had very minimal problems with her, and her character development could be seen. And Kai was the star of this book—he made scenes with Kitt bearable, and honestly, he and Paedyn really aced this book, made it out to be a more enjoyable experience than it could've been.

The plot, honestly, I really liked how the first and second trial went by. It made it feel more enjoyable and reduced the repetitive nature of the book, but the third one dragged. The whole incest thing put me off so bad because it was just so disgusting. There were intimate thoughts and scenes, so it was just very off-putting for me. The writing was inconsistent at times. Again, the plot twists were poorly executed. Some things were done very well, but they didn't outweigh the things that didn't. And honestly, the inconsistent pacing + the repeating nature of Kai's nicknames for Paedyn also annoyed me. If you can overlook these things, I do believe it could be a really good experience, but for me it was tainted because these hindered my experience a lot and I could not enjoy it fully which is sad because this book had immense potential.

This honestly is her best work after Powerful lol.

4.5⭐️ I genuinely don’t know if I can properly put into words what this book did to me. I’m feeling all the emotions. My eyes hurt. I’ve been staring at my wall for like 20 minutes just contemplating life.

Listen after hating Reckless I wasn’t even sure that I was going to read this and oh my god am I so happy I did!!! THIS WAS EVERYTHING I NEEDED AND MORE!!! Is this series going to be for everyone? No absolutely not, I feel like you’re either gonna love or hate it, and I was scared I was gonna turn into a certified hater after reckless but NOPEEEEEEEEEE, I feel like Lauren Robert’s took all my issue I had with reckless and wrote fearless and said BET…. Let me prove you wrong.

This isn’t a heavy fantasy read, the romance is the absolutely the main focus so also know that going in… but Kai and Pae actually own my soul at this point so like….. actually they own pieces of my jagged heart because WHAT THE FUCK I HAVE WHIPLASH!!!! I’m actually in severe emotional turmoil.

THE ANGST. The longing. The tension. THE YEARNING?!!!!!!! Kai Azer. KAI AZER. No. Stop. This man had me in absolute SHAMBLES!!! Idk how but Lauren Robert’s somehow made him even better in this book. I’m sick. His complete and utter devotion to Pae had me on my knees.

Pae and Kai’s romance in this was everything I was hoping for! The forbidden aspect, the push and pull, them giving in to their love for one another!! I felt like this was the most their chemistry shined and it was so palpable! I felt like in reckless their love wasn’t believable, that was so not the case here! My heart broke right along with theirs. I love how both of them was sacrifice everything for the other.

Pae isn’t my favorite FMC, but I grew to love her in this book despite her royally pissing me off at points. I felt like she went through some much needed growth and her confidence in herself made me feel like a proud mom. But again… she did still piss me off, WHY DIDNT YOU JUST RUN AWAY WITH KAI?!!! Why did you go through with marrying kitt?!!!!!! Pissed me off so bad.

Now listen, was the plot revolutionary? No, but like for me personally…. I GOBBLED IT UP! I loved that she had to go through trials again, I felt like it was super fast paced and easy to get lost in! Also the amount of plot twists that I never saw coming that had my jaw on the floor….. I’m still speechless. Kit and Pae being half siblings was not on my Fearless bingo card and it’s actually hilarious to me. Haters are gonna reach and say there was incest in here… BFFR. Idk maybe I just read too much dark romance but I loved how blindsided I was by this and how shocked it had me, I also just thought it was so funny. Also the fact that they all just acknowledged it literally one time and moved on…. DEAD.

Small issues I had that made me incapable of giving this 5 stars:
- Lauren did Mak so dirty, I’m so bitter that did not need to happen, I understand he’s at peace now with Adena but like IM NOT!!! I’m suffering.
- It was pretty clear that Kit was sick and most likely dying early on…. But I hated how Kai was the one to ultimately take his life. Like why did you do that to my sweet baby angel Kai?! Hasn’t he suffered enough?!
- Ending was just a little rushed.

All in all I absolutely loved this. I highlighted almost every word that came out of Kai’s mouth. These quotes made me pass away.

“She is the single most destructive thing I have ever desired, and yet, it is the diamond on her finger that will destroy me.”

“Paedyn is not a right or a wrong, not something as simple as a yes or a no. She is confusion itself, a feeling unplaced, a color between black and white.”

“I could fall to my knees, beg to be the only one worthy of witnessing her.”

“I’m breathless at the sight of her, doomed by the hope of having her. It’s a beautiful ruin, a devastating devotion. This girl holds my heart in her hands, could crush it between her fingers and still have me thanking her for the touch.”

“My name means nothing to me until she speaks it. Nothing until she claims it as her own.”

“My favorite color is a shade of her, a sliver of the vibrance she exudes. And I will gladly drown, gladly burn, gladly fall into those blue eyes until the day she looks at me for the last time.”

“So if you leave, I will follow. If you stay, I will bow. Because there has never been a moment when you did not own the only piece of me that mattered—loving you made me matter. And I ache to be full again.”

“You don’t need a blade. I would bleed if only you asked.”

“She is a vision, something so ethereal in this moment that I may just believe there is a God. She is the closest thing to a deity.”

what the hell is this series.

when i first read powerless, i just thought it was giving wattpad hunger games with a little harry potter and the selection thrown in. didn’t love it, but fine, i played along. and then i started seeing reviews. actual breakdowns of scenes and characters and worldbuilding and how deeply this series rips off red queen. and i haven’t even read red queen, and it’s still painfully obvious. now we’re copying the serpent and the wings of night too? be so serious.

how is no one talking about how this is basically plagiarism in plain sight???

nothing in this series is original. not the world, not the characters, not the romance, not even the twists. it’s like a ya fantasy frankenstein stitched together from better stories and dressed up in viral tiktok aesthetics. if this were indie, everyone would be tearing it to shreds by page 10. but because it’s shiny and trad pub, it somehow gets a free pass???

the writing is actually the worst part. you can feel it trying to go viral. every other line is a “quote-worthy” moment engineered to sound good on an audiobook edit. no weight, no meaning, just vibes and sparkles and kai saying pretty things in his sad emo boy voice.

plot? what plot. it’s just one shock twist after another with no logic or build-up. and they’re not even good twists—they’re purely for shock value, and they contradict the books that came before them. like girl, you’re not clever, you’re just doing the most and hoping no one notices it’s a mess.

also. the cheating arc. WHY is that okay because it’s the main couple??? why are we acting like that plotline wasn’t gross.

and let’s talk about kai for a second. i wanted to like him. i really did. but he’s not a character anymore, he’s just a quote machine. poetic sad emo boy with abs:(

this book genuinely made me laugh—not because it was funny, but because i could not believe how unserious it was. like… this passed through editors??? actual professionals thought this was good to go???

powerless felt like fanfic. reckless was straight filler. fearless is just bad.

i’m tired. i’m so tired.

this series is a scam. and you cannot convince me otherwise.

”Damn fate, and duty, and every other word meant to keep us apart.” Tears slip from those blue eyes I would happily drown in. “I want to hide with you beneath the willow tree. I love Pae so much.
She is such a strong character and I never find her annoying or anything. She has been through so much and I admire her strength and that she still has the ability to deeply care for things around her. I really liked how she started healing in this book and how she started thinking about Adena not with sadness, but with joy that she had her in the first place. She had so many badass moments and quotes. Her backstory was actually insane and I love how she dealt with it. I’m actually not that mad about Blair, but I’ll talk about that later :)

⤷MY BABY GOT A HAPPY ENDING

When he died i literally cried so hard, I swear my parents probably thought i was insane as they heard me screaming “no!” through the walls. It might just have been the ugliest sob of my life.

⤷ “I am no one’s queen.”

“You seem to forget that I’m completely powerless, Prince.”

“And you the muse, darling.”

⤷ “Oh, my pretty Pae.” His words are a murmur against my lips. “For once, it is I who will be your undoing.”

⤷ “I will show you my bravery, my benevolence, my brutality. I will survive these Trials and so much more. Still, you will likely hate me.” She lifts her chin, expression deceitfully calm. “So bow at my feet and sneer, if you must. I won’t see it with your face on the ground.”

⤷ “If you want me to fight you, I won’t, Paedyn. I told you in that field of poppies how I would never do that again. That when I lay a hand on you, it would only ever be in a caress.” Raindrops drip from his lashes, but he doesn’t care blink as he murmurs, “And I plan to keep that vow.”

⤷ “My pretty, pretty Pae.” She laughs breathlessly. “Stay with me.”

⤷ “I was prepared to plead.”

⤷ “You know,” she says slowly, “you’re not nearly as terrifying as you seem.”
“Not to you. Never to you.”

⤷ “My favorite color is the shade of her, a sliver of the vibrancy she excludes. And I will gladly drown, gladly burn, gladly fall into those blue eyes until the day she looks at me for the last time.”

KAI AZER
kai is truly amazing. i've never hated him and i love him. he's like a very selfless character and throughout this series, i've seen him do nothing wrong. in this book, he was still considerate about everything. ugh i don't have much to say about him. i loved his bond with kitt.

KITT AZER
now, i'll end this review with the mention of this beautiful boy who's done so wrong. i'm sorry i found you boring in book 2, you were simply grieving. Kitt is such a complex character, and throughout this book, his behavior with paedyn was indifferent but pretty valid. i did kinda feel frustrated as to why he's marrying her even after knowing kai loves her a lot, but his feelings are messy, and that’s what makes him so real.

man simply wanted his father to love him. he wanted someone to love him. and kai did. i believe kitt loved kai so fucking much, even though it was borderline obsessive during the last moments. i know that's because of the plague or whatever. Kitt's character is written so complicatedly, i literally couldn't hate him. had he been callous about hating paedyn and wanting to kill her, i would've understood. he was never a monster. he never wanted to kill her/hate her; he simply wanted someone to love him. reading his letters in the end had my heart aching. i truly, genuinely felt so much pity and bad for him, i can't explain. he's such a pure character and is NOT done justice. but the fact that in the afterlife he did get his peace—that's the only thing making me feel kind of better.

as for kai & paedyn's love story, i'm glad they got their end, but they truly lost me in the end. I honestly don't care enough to come back. this series started off good but it's NOT, not anymore.

➳ 3/5 stars
➳“I’m breathless at the sight of her, doomed by the hope of having her. It’s a beautiful ruin, a devastating devotion. This girl holds my heart in her hands, could crush it between her fingers and still have me thanking her for the touch."
Sooo guess what? This book failed to deliver, again. I was genuinely excited for it. Okay, maybe not a painfully long wait, but I was definitely eager to get my hands on it. I had hopes, expectations, a little bit of desperate faith, and Lauren just… didn’t come through. The amount of absurdity packed into this book had me rolling my eyes so many times I was worried they’d get stuck. At one point, I literally called it bullshit out loud.

Now, I get that some people probably loved the ending, and I respect that, but for me? It just wasn’t it. This was supposed to be the finale, the big conclusion to the series. I had sky-high expectations, and it didn’t even come close. I can kinda see how the twists might've worked for some readers, but personally, they were so predictable it hurt. And to make matters worse, I got spoiled for the major twist (IYKYK), which had me fuming.

Like, this book is 600 pages. I usually don’t mind long reads, but I was already deep in a slump and dragging myself through it was hard enough. Then, boom spoiler hits me because someone can’t be bothered to slap a spoiler warning on their post. How hard is it, seriously? After that, I pretty much lost all motivation to keep reading. Took me a whole month to finally pick it back up, and even then, it felt more like a chore than something I was excited to finish.

All in all, it had so much potential… and it just didn’t live up to it. Disappointed but not surprised.

➳ ABOUT THE BOOK

So apparently, this book picks up right where the last one left off, with Kai dragging Pae back to the Kitt so she can face punishment for her so-called crimes. But plot twist? Kitt suddenly decides to marry her and make her queen. Yeah… I know, make it make sense, but just stay with me here. From that point on, the story pretty much spins in circles. The entire book is just a dramatic love letter to how deeply Kai loves Pae (which, to be fair, is very sweet), and how they're both meant to survive being apart while pretending none of it hurts.

We’re also meant to care about how this whole royal mess is supposed to work, how Pae’s marriage to Kitt will affect the kingdom, how Kitt plans to rule without the old king’s guidance, etc. But none of it really lands with the weight it’s supposed to. Sure, there were a few twists sprinkled in, but honestly? They weren’t as mind-blowing or gasp-worthy as I hoped.

It felt like the book was just looping around the same emotional beats, over and over. You know the kind where you keep turning pages thinking something big’s about to happen… but it never really does? Yeah, that.


➳ ABOUT THE CHARACTERS

* SPOILER ALERT *

see now was it so hard? anyways, let’s talk about the characters again because honestly, this book was entirely carried by my beloved Kai Azer. Yes, he had his moments where I couldn’t help but roll my eyes at what he was saying, but we’re going to politely ignore that, because when you stack him up next to the rest of the cast… oh boy, he shines like gold in a pile of very questionable choices. And my heart hurts for this boy because he didn't deserved half of the shit he went through.

Starting with Miss Paedyn Gray, what happened to her? She was an absolute standout in the first book. I adored her. But in this one? She just didn’t feel like the same girl. Sure, she had her signature badass moments, and some of them did hit. But a lot of it felt like the author was desperately trying to keep up her tough-girl image, throwing in scenes that felt more performative than powerful. Half the time I was laughing, not because it was funny, but because it was so forced.

And then there’s Kitt. Oh, Kitt. I genuinely don’t know how you take a character I actually liked in the first book and turn him into this. For everyone out there still supporting Kitt, bless your heart, you do you.

But for me? I simply can’t wrap my head around his choices. This man knew Kai’s mother was dying and still sent him off to retrieve Pae, like it couldn’t wait a few days? Knowing full well he was risking Kai not getting the chance to say goodbye? That’s not just cold, it’s cruel.

And let’s not forget, he was so desperate to be better than his father that he ended up being… somehow worse. Like, King Edric created the plague, we get that. It was horrific. So why on earth would Kitt bring it back? And test it? On himself? The math is not mathing. He was so obsessed with being seen, with being powerful, with leaving a mark, that he stopped caring who he hurt along the way. Kai and Pae both suffered because of his decisions, and don’t even get me started on how shady those trials were.

Lauren, we loved the trials in book one, yes. But not everything needs a comeback. These new ones? They were irrelevant at best, frustrating at worst.

Kitt didn’t even feel like the same man. Gone was the sweet, charming boy from book one. In his place was someone so blinded by jealousy and power that he couldn't even grasp the damage he was causing. I get it—he was manipulated by Callum—but he still had choices. And he made the worst ones every time. I’ve genuinely never come across a character who was so hell-bent on chasing greatness that he didn’t care what it cost, especially when that cost was the very people who once trusted him most.

And now… Callum. Oh my god. First of all, a huge fuck you to whoever spoiled that he was pae’s father. Like, seriously? That twist had the potential to actually shake things up, and someone just had to go and ruin it. And i was already side-eyeing Callum before I even fully met him. But even without the spoiler, I despised his character. There was just something off about him from the beginning, this eerie vibe that made me not want to trust a single thing he said. I mean, how can I possibly like a man who can literally read your thoughts? That is not just creepy, it’s downright disturbing.

And don’t even get me started on the whole Pae situation. I had my suspicions the moment they said her alleged father adam was a healer and yet she somehow ended up completely powerless. I mean… what? Even if we didn’t know much about her dead mother’s powers, the chances of her being born entirely powerless when her father’s got a gift? Slim . But then, boom, turns out she’s actually Callum’s daughter? And her mother wasn't Adam's dead wife but the Queen Iris herself? And BOTH her parents are ridiculously powerful. And she’s still powerless? Be for real.

Yes, I know this is fantasy and authors can bend the rules, but there’s still a thing called internal logic. And this twist just broke all the rules we were told to follow. If you set up a world with magical genetics, you kinda have to stick to the rules you built. Otherwise, it just feels like the author’s pulling random plot twists out of a hat.

➳ FINAL THOUGHTS

While I definitely had my own little issue with this book, I can totally understand why some readers absolutely adore it. It had its moments, and I won’t deny that. But for me? It just didn’t hit the spot the way I hoped it would. Some things felt off,like, I get that this is the big finale, the dramatic conclusion, the moment we’ve all been waiting for. But instead of leaving me with that emotional, bittersweet goodbye I crave from the final book of series, it kind of left me questioning why I even started this series in the first place.

I’m usually cautious with hyped books, I’ve been burned before, but when literally everyone and their mother was obsessed with this series, I thought, “Okay, let me give it a try.” And now here I am, regretting that choice and lowkey laughing at my own expectations.

That said, I will give credit where it’s due: Lauren’s writing is still masterful. She has a gift, no doubt. Her prose, her ability to draw emotion from a single glance or line, it’s all there. But the plot? It just didn’t hold up this time. Somewhere along the way, things started to feel repetitive. It was like déjà vu in book form, I honestly felt like I was reading the first book all over again.

And please… the word “pretend.” I don’t think I’ve ever been haunted by a word the way this book haunted me with that one. It was used so many times I started twitching every time it popped up. Like, there are synonyms, my friend. Let’s diversify a little. The constant mentions of eye colors also had me groaning, like, how many times can we admire the same pair of eyes before it becomes a running joke?

And don’t even get me started on the plot twists,I’ve already talked more than enough about those. Let’s just say I wasn’t shocked so much as mildly annoyed.

°˖➴ "Overall, if you’re looking for a fantasy book that leans toward the mediocre side, but has a swoonworthy male lead to carry you through, then hey, maybe this is your thing."💌

So if you leave, I will follow. If you stay, I will bow. Because there has never been a moment when you did not own the only piece of me that mattered—loving you made me matter. And I ache to be full again."

3.5 stars ⭐
⤷ spoiler-free unless stated otherwise!! ⋆౨ৎ˚⟡˖ ࣪

despite reckless being a letdown, i still held onto that sliver of hope that Lauren Roberts would redeem the trilogy with this final installment. unfortunately, that hope was misplaced—fearless ended up being yet another disappointment.

the beginning felt a little boring, and the dynamic between paedyn and kai felt repetitive and stale. i’ll give credit where it’s due: the plot twists were unpredictable, but dumping all the major revelations at the end threw the pacing off and left the story feeling rushed and chaotic.

🚨 MAJOR SPOILERS AHEAD 🚨





so you’re telling me all of this drama happened because king edric believed his ordinary daughter—who, plot twist, wasn’t even his biological daughter—was responsible for his wife’s death? 🤦🏻‍♀️

anyhoo, here’s a breakdown of what didn’t work for me:

1. the trials: they felt like they were thrown in just to fill pages rather than drive the plot forward. for something that was meant to be high-stakes, they came off as lackluster and half-hearted.

2. mak: I AM RIOTING FOR A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT REASON. Ms. Lauren Roberts… WHY TF WOULD YOU KILL HIM OFF LIKE THAT?! he had so much potential and it felt like he was being set up for something bigger. his death was abrupt, unnecessary, and easily the biggest letdown in the book.

3. paedyn and kai: i adore them, i really do, but they lost that spark that once made them one of my favourite fictional couples. the constant “i love you but we can’t be together” and “this is just pretend” cycle dragged on way too long, it felt like their relationship was stuck in a loop. #packitup!!!

4. the plot twists: finding out that paedyn’s biological father was calum—and that she and kitt were half-siblings—was CRAZY, but the tangled web of bloodlines and secret family ties were so convoluted, i had to physically put the book down a few times just to mentally map it all out.

5. kitt: oh, kitt. i’ve defended him since book one, but his character arc in this one really disappointed me. i spent all this time thinking he was in love with paedyn and jealous of kai, only to find out he was jealous of paedyn?! his obsession with kai was pretty bizarre (but it makes sense given how unhinged he was), and his death was even more ridiculous. like wdym he forgot to dodge??? 😭





END OF SPOILERS

overall, while this wasn’t a terrible book, it was definitely a disappointing conclusion to a trilogy that started off with so much promise. what began as something truly special to me ended in disappointment, and i wish i could say otherwise 😪 (can you tell how disappointed i am?)

ˏˋ°•*⁀➷ the powerless trilogy

♡.ᐟ powerful 🌌 (5 ⭐)
♡.ᐟ reckless 🌹🌿 (3.75 ⭐)
♡.ᐟ fearless 👑🩸 (3.5 ⭐)

this review is going to be a jumbled up mess of thoughts ⚠️ full of spoilers, that will probably make no sense whatsoever


── .❀ 𝔪𝔶 𝔱𝔥𝔬𝔲𝔤𝔥𝔱𝔰


lauren roberts fr rearranged the whole family tree with this one.

sooooo… where to start. i know that i say that books break me all the time, but i don’t think i’ve ever been this broken. like, i haven’t had a response to a book like this since liam mairi from fourth wing. my hands haven’t stopped shaking and i finished an over an hour ago. i think i actually put the most of plot together around 30% and i FINALLY understood what was going to happen, but i was still surprised just to see it on paper. KITT MY BABY IM SO SORRY.


before we get into the good stuff, do yall remember that chapter where kai and kitt and pae all dance together?? where paedyn makes it a tradition that they all dance together?

i just realized that’s the first and last time they ever get to do that tradition.

let me cry for a minute.


and they had a baby girl and named her kit 🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹 my heart omg

i think that’s lauren’s writing and world building has definitely improved since powerless, which is saying something because powerless is one of my faves. the only thing that was king of lacking was the plot. the first half was pretty slow, and it felt like a repeat of book 1, especially with the trials.


── .❀ 𝔎𝔦𝔱𝔱𝔶
i swear to god, if diehard powerless fans start hating on kitt, it will be the end of me. he was literally just a boy who wanted people to love him for who he was. but he felt lonely, so he changed himself to get that power. in a my own way, i guess i can relate to him, so that last chapter… ugh.

time of death: the epilogue

i mean- i might have to reread it again just to fully get the part about the actual plague (i rushed it because i had a dentist appt. like, how fucking dare they rip me from my book. i only see them every 6 months, and they chose now???). he’s just a boy who loved the wrong girl. he’s just a boy with a parent who never fully appreciated who he was. even in death, he’ll be known as the one who was unhinged, but his story is just so sad. *sniffles*


── .❀ 𝔭𝔯𝔢𝔱𝔱𝔶 𝔭𝔞𝔢
i loved seeing how paedyn grew into her role more. it was kind of painful seeing her trying to make up with kitt, even though there was something clearly wrong with him. paedyn is a bit of a drama queen when she wants to be, but overall, we love her.


── .❀ 𝔎𝔞𝔦 𝔭𝔦𝔢
hot morally Gray (get it?) man in the houseeee!!!! 🗣️🗣️🗣️ enough with the bad puns, i couldn’t help myself. anyway. kai is of course, hot as always. he did get more… sentimental?? he said a lot more cheesy stuff in this book.

you can honestly tell that this man was written by a women, because yeah, he’s kind of perfect.

speaking of which, i kind of hate him, because why did he ruin all real men for me?? not only did this book shatter me, but now i’ll never look at nonfictional men the same?? great. 🤦‍♀️🤦‍♀️🤦‍♀️


── .❀ 𝔟𝔦𝔱𝔠𝔥𝔶 𝔟𝔩𝔞𝔦𝔯
WHO THE FUCK LET BLAIR LIVE?? i may be a complete bitch, but still i refuse to feel bad about blair’s face. i mean, she deserved it. my girl adena deserved better. plus, she thought she could have kai. anyway, i do hold a bit of respect for her but…

i hope she rots in hell. eventually 🥰🥰

── .❀ 𝔟𝔦𝔤 𝔪𝔞𝔨
i haven’t read powerful, BUT MAK JUST DIED IN FRONT OF ME TRYING TO GET TO ADENA. her “slums boy”. what the hell. just another one of the many ways that i was broken. like-

── .❀ 𝔠𝔞𝔩𝔲𝔪
i cannot believe this man right now. her father!! i swear, all the good ones have daddy issues 🫠🫠

── .❀ 𝔟𝔯𝔞𝔤𝔤𝔦𝔫𝔤 𝔯𝔦𝔤𝔥𝔱𝔰
the cover. so i know that going into this one, we were all speculating about the cover. i would just like to brag for a second, because i was right??? with those bloody rose petals?? please. anyway. i’m done bragging. i’ll be serious again.

jinx. i’m not done. so, i think i figured the plot out around 30% and i was like 99.99% what was going to happen, but seeing it written on paper was a whole different story. like, my mind was blown even though i knew what was going to happen. annnddd i also managed to avoid all spoilers, so congrats to me 🎉🎉
